transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because things just got a little out of hand lately. 

I was barely settling into my new apartment, and then... I don't know, I just suddenly started saying yes to all these mentoring sessions. And taking on extra client prototypes for work. I even started redesigning my whole portfolio. It was just... like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint, I guess. So... yeah. That's why I came in.
How long has this period of feeling like you needed to take on all these extra projects and 'fix everything' been going on—days, weeks, or longer?
Um... I'd say it's been about a month. Ever since I moved into the new place. It's just been... this whole up-and-down thing since then.
During this past month, have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy the next day?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... for a few nights there, I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours. But I didn't really feel tired. I just woke up thinking I was totally fine... so I figured I should just use the extra time to get ahead on things.
Before this past month, have you ever had a period—lasting two weeks or more—where you felt unusually sad, low, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um... yeah. I suppose so. The... heavier stretches of feeling like that, they've been showing up since... well, since a separation about 11 months ago. That was before this latest move kind of made everything sharper. But... yeah.

During that month when you were taking on all these extra projects and sleeping less, did it cause any serious problems—like conflicts at work, trouble with relationships, or needing to be hospitalized—or were you still able to manage your daily responsibilities?

Um... I wasn't in the hospital or anything like that. But... I guess it did cause some issues. I, um... I missed a design review at work. Just completely spaced on it. And... I haven't really been talking to my friends or family much. I've just been... avoiding them, I suppose. It's just embarrassing, really... how scattered and unreliable I've been.
During that month, did you ever experience any unusual beliefs, racing thoughts you couldn't control, or see/hear things that others didn't, or feel like you completely lost touch with what was real?
No... no, nothing like that. Just... my thoughts were moving fast, I guess, but I always knew what was real. I didn't see anything that wasn't there.

This narrows the diagnosis to Bipolar I, current episode manic without psychotic symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a distinct one-month period of elevated, goal-directed behavior (over-scheduling mentoring sessions, extra work projects, redesigning her portfolio), decreased need for sleep (3-4 hours without fatigue), and subjective racing thoughts. This period caused clear functional impairment—missing a work review and withdrawing from friends/family—meeting criteria for a manic (not merely hypomanic) episode. No psychotic features (hallucinations, delusions, loss of reality contact) were present, and there was no hospitalization. A prior major depressive episode (following a separation ~11 months ago) confirms a bipolar course, supporting Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic, without psychotic features (F31.1) over Bipolar II (which would require only hypomania without functional impairment) or unipolar depression.
